sections.overview: This South American snake belongs to the Chironius multiventris species complex, still under taxonomic revision.
sections.identification: It has a brown back, yellow mottling on its lower sides and strongly keeled dorsal scales.
sections.habitat: It occurs in Bolivia’s Beni savanna and Chiquitano Dry Forest, with one confirmed record in Brazil’s Rondônia.
sections.diet: Frog records suggest more terrestrial habits than in some relatives.
sections.behavior: A Bolivian field guide says little is known and records observations mainly in August and October.
sections.reproduction: The 2026 study records juveniles in January–April but gives no clutch size or exact laying dates.
sections.ecology: Its closest named sister is C. xaraes; they occupy separate river basins.
sections.conservation: The revision gives no population estimate or global threat category.
